SSME blades are subject to severe thermal, pressure, and forced vibration environments.
SSME/STAEBL is a stand-alone code for automated design of SSME turbopump blades, developed by modifying and enhancing the STAEBL code.
Typical design variables in SSME/STAEBL include blade thickness distribution and root chord.
Typical constraints include resonance margins, root stress, and root-to-chord ratios.
Additions and modifications in SSME/STAEBL include thermal stress analysis, gas dynamic loads, temperature-dependent properties, forced vibrations, and blade cross-section stacking offsets.
Optimization studies showed that including thermal and pressure loads, as well as temperature-dependent properties, requires additional weight in the optimized design to meet all constraints.
Crystal axis orientation had a relatively small effect on the optimal design of a single-crystal SSME turbopump blade, which was dominated by a root stress constraint.
Blade cross-section stacking offsets were shown to have a very significant effect on root stress-dominated designs.
The natural frequencies of the optimized SSME turbopump blade design under centrifugal loads only were 3562, 3854, 4383, 4866, and 7916 Hz.
The root stress of the optimized SSME turbopump blade design under centrifugal loads only was 106 ksi, compared to 83 ksi for the initial design.
The root stress of the optimized SSME turbopump blade design under centrifugal, thermal, and pressure loads with temperature-dependent properties was 65 ksi.
The blade weight of the optimized SSME turbopump blade design under centrifugal loads only was 3.14 lb, compared to 3.0 lb for the initial design.

The optimized SSME turbopump blade design under centrifugal, thermal, and pressure loads with temperature-dependent properties had a tip displacement of 0.209 in, compared to 0.0027 in for the design optimized under centrifugal loads only.

The forced response margin for the optimized SSME turbopump blade design under centrifugal, thermal, and pressure loads with temperature-dependent properties was 0.010, compared to 0.000 for the design optimized under centrifugal loads only.

The stage weight of the optimized SSME turbopump blade design under centrifugal, thermal, and pressure loads with temperature-dependent properties was 4.15 lb, compared to 3.0 lb for the design optimized under centrifugal loads only.
